name: copd-shelved-drugs
note: COPD drug programs that failed a primary endpoint or were judged not worth pursuing in COPD. Every fact is from the cited source; 'not stated in sources' marks gaps. Company is given only where a cited source names it. No source after 2025. phase_reached is null where the source doesn't state a phase. Each source has a type: academic, company, regulatory_filing or news.

drugs.pathway: CXCR2 antagonist (oral): blocks neutrophil recruitment to the lung
drugs.status: Phase 2b: no benefit on symptoms; authors judged benefit-risk unfavorable
drugs.reason: No dose improved E-RS:COPD symptom scores vs placebo at month 6 (large placebo effect); more exacerbations on danirixin (56-75 per arm vs 44 on placebo).
drugs.side_effects: Pneumonia more frequent at 50 mg (5%) than placebo (<1%); all serious pneumonia events were in danirixin arms.

sources.title: CXCR2 antagonist for patients with COPD with chronic mucus hypersecretion: a phase 2b trial (Respiratory Research)

drugs.status: Exacerbation study stopped early at interim analysis; phase 2 cardiovascular study negative
drugs.reason: Exacerbation rate ratio vs placebo 1.04 (95% CrI 0.63-1.73); study terminated for low probability of success. Separate 16-week trial: no effect on arterial inflammation or endothelial function.
drugs.side_effects: No new safety signals in the exacerbation study; in the 16-week trial serious adverse events were more frequent on losmapimod (mostly COPD exacerbations and pneumonia).

sources.title: Biological effects of p38 MAPK inhibitor losmapimod does not translate to clinical benefits in COPD
The p38 MAPK inhibitor losmapimod in COPD patients with systemic inflammation, stratified by fibrinogen (PLOS ONE)

drugs.reason: No difference in FEV1 change at week 12 vs placebo (750 ug vs placebo -0.004 L) and no difference in re-exacerbations (n=938).

sources.title: Nemiralisib in Patients with an Acute Exacerbation of COPD: Placebo-Controlled, Dose-Ranging Study

drugs.status: Early study: target engaged but no anti-inflammatory effect; authors conclude PI3K delta is not a suitable COPD pathway
drugs.reason: 29.7% reduction in sputum PIP3 (target engagement) did not translate into any anti-inflammatory pharmacodynamic effect.
drugs.side_effects: Cough in 95.2% of patients, mostly mild to moderate, resolving within an hour of dosing.

sources.title: CHF6523 data suggest that the PI3K delta isoform is not a suitable target for the management of COPD

drugs.pathway: IL-5 receptor alpha-directed cytolytic antibody: depletes eosinophils
drugs.status: Three phase 3 trials missed their primary endpoint: GALATHEA and TERRANOVA (2018-2019) and RESOLUTE (2025); AstraZeneca said it will analyse the full RESOLUTE data
drugs.reason: No dose significantly reduced annualized exacerbations vs placebo at week 56 in patients with eosinophils >=220/uL (rate ratios 0.83-1.04). RESOLUTE (n=689, eosinophils >=300/uL, 3 or more exacerbations in the prior year): numerical improvement but no statistically significant reduction in exacerbations.
drugs.side_effects: Types and frequencies of adverse events similar to placebo. RESOLUTE: safety and tolerability consistent with the known profile.

sources.title: Phase 3 trial of benralizumab for COPD misses primary endpoint (HCPLive)
Benralizumab for the Prevention of COPD Exacerbations (NEJM)
AstraZeneca: Update on the RESOLUTE Phase III trial for Fasenra in COPD

drugs.status: Phase 3 ARNASA missed primary endpoint (phase 2b ALIENTO met it); Roche to discuss next steps with regulators
drugs.reason: ARNASA (n=1,375): 14.5% numerical reduction in annualized exacerbations, not significant; ALIENTO (n=1,301): 15.4%, significant. Exacerbations lower than anticipated in both.

sources.title: Roche provides update on astegolimab in COPD
Genentech (Roche)'s Astegolimab Shows Mixed Data for COPD (HCPLive)

drugs.status: Phase 3 mixed: AERIFY-1 met primary endpoint, AERIFY-2 did not; companies to discuss path forward with regulators
drugs.reason: AERIFY-2 exacerbation reduction at week 52: 2% (every 2 weeks) and 12% (every 4 weeks), not significant; AERIFY-1: 27% and 21%, significant. Fewer exacerbations than anticipated reduced power.
drugs.side_effects: Adverse events comparable to placebo (AERIFY-1: 67% and 68% vs 68%; AERIFY-2: 64% and 71% vs 64%).

sources.title: Sanofi Form 6-K exhibit: itepekimab phase 3 COPD results
Itepekimab Shows Mixed Results in Phase 3 COPD Trials (AJMC)

drugs.status: Phase 2b: primary endpoint negative; later development: not stated in sources
drugs.reason: No dose-response for trough FEV1 at week 12 (primary endpoint); some improvements at week 24 that the authors say must be interpreted with caution.

sources.title: Icenticaftor, a CFTR Potentiator, in COPD: A Multicenter, Parallel-Group, Double-Blind Clinical Trial

drugs.status: Phase 2 in COPD: no improvement; authors call for dose-finding studies
drugs.reason: Did not improve sweat chloride, mucociliary clearance, lung function or symptoms over 12 weeks (n=40); drug exposure was lower than in cystic fibrosis.
drugs.side_effects: Most common adverse event on ivacaftor: diarrhea; adverse event rates similar to placebo.

sources.title: Ivacaftor for COPD: Results from a Phase 2, Randomized Controlled Trial
